title: Jump and Link (jal) and Return (jr) Execution
description: Trace how jal jumps to a procedure label and saves the return address in $ra so jr $ra can resume main.

steps.description: In `main`, load `4` into argument register `$a0` and execute `jal procedure` to jump to `procedure` while saving the return address in `$ra`.
At `procedure`, add 1 to `$a0` and store the result in `$v0`, then jump back to the caller with `jr $ra` so `main` can load `10` into `$v0` and exit via `syscall`.
Notice how `jal procedure` and `jr $ra` work as a pair: `jal` records the address of the instruction after line 8 in `$ra`, and `jr $ra` jumps back to that saved address.

steps.question: What value does `addi $v0, $a0, 1` place in `$v0` before `jr $ra` returns to `main`?
steps.answer: 5, because `$a0` holds 4 and `addi` adds 1 to it.

steps.description: `jal procedure` has jumped to line 15 and saved the return address in `$ra`; line 15 now computes `$v0 = $a0 + 1` (5).
`jr $ra` returns control to line 11 in `main`, which loads syscall code 10 into `$v0` to exit.
